questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which is the largest lake in Uganda?
questions.explanation: Lake Victoria is the largest lake in Uganda and in Africa.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: In which part of Uganda is Mount Rwenzori found?
questions.explanation: Mount Rwenzori lies in western Uganda, on the border with the D.R. Congo.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The highest peak of Mount Rwenzori is called ______ peak.
questions.explanation: Margherita is the highest peak of Mount Rwenzori.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Lake Albert was formed mainly by ______.
questions.explanation: Lake Albert lies in the Rift Valley, which was formed by faulting.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which type of climate is found around Lake Victoria?
questions.explanation: The Lake Victoria area has an equatorial climate: warm with rain most of the year.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which part of Uganda receives the least rainfall?
questions.explanation: Karamoja is semi-arid, so it gets little and unreliable rainfall.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which vegetation type covers most of Karamoja?
options: B. Savanna grassland with thorny bushes
questions.explanation: Dry savanna with thorny bushes suits areas with low rainfall like Karamoja.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which soil type is best for growing most crops?
questions.explanation: Loam soil holds water well and is rich in plant food.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Copper used to be mined at ______ in Kasese district.
questions.explanation: Kilembe mines in Kasese are known for copper.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Limestone used for making cement is mined at ______.
questions.explanation: Tororo has limestone deposits used in the cement industry.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Growing crops mainly for selling is called ______ farming.
questions.explanation: Commercial farming produces for sale; subsistence farming is for the family.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which cash crop grows best on the slopes of Mount Elgon?
questions.explanation: The cool, high slopes of Mt Elgon suit Arabica coffee.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which lake supplies the largest amount of fish in Uganda?
questions.explanation: Lake Victoria is Uganda's biggest source of fish.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why is fishing using poison discouraged?
options: B. It kills young fish and pollutes the water
questions.explanation: Poison kills fish of all sizes and makes the water unsafe.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The official counting of all people in a country is called a population ______.
questions.explanation: A census counts people and collects information for planning.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: An area with very many people living in it is said to be ______.
questions.explanation: Densely populated means many people live in a small area.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why do many people settle near lakes?
options: B. There is water, fish and fertile soil
questions.explanation: Water, fish and fertile soils attract settlement.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Who is the political head of a district in Uganda?
questions.explanation: The LC V chairperson is the elected political head of a district.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Uganda got her independence in the year ______.
questions.explanation: Uganda became independent on 9th October 1962.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: At what age can a Ugandan citizen vote in national elections?
questions.explanation: Ugandans aged 18 years and above are allowed to vote.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The part of a map that explains what the symbols mean is called the ______.
questions.explanation: The key (or legend) explains the symbols used on a map.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: On a map with a scale of 1:50,000, one centimetre represents ______ on the ground.
questions.explanation: 1 cm stands for 50,000 cm, and 50,000 cm is 500 metres.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The direction exactly between North and East is called ______.
questions.explanation: North East lies halfway between North and East.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Planting trees in an area where there were no trees before is called ______.
questions.explanation: Afforestation is planting new forest; replanting a cut forest is reafforestation.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why should swamps be protected?
options: A. They dry up the land
B. They filter water and hold it during dry seasons
questions.explanation: Wetlands clean water, store it and are home to many living things.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which ministry is responsible for schools in Uganda?
options: B. Ministry of Education and Sports
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Education and Sports runs education in Uganda.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A dispensary is one of the places where people get health services.
questions.explanation: Dispensaries, health centres and hospitals all provide health services.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The railway line built from Mombasa towards Kampala is called the ______ Railway.
questions.explanation: It was named the Uganda Railway although it started at Mombasa.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Buying goods from other countries is called ______.
questions.explanation: Importation is buying from abroad; exportation is selling abroad.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Match each physical feature with where it is found.
questions.explanation: Knowing where features are helps you read maps of Uganda.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A farmer on a steep hill is losing soil whenever it rains. What should he do?
options: B. Dig terraces across the slope
questions.explanation: Terraces slow down running water so it cannot wash away soil.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which one is a renewable natural resource?
questions.explanation: Forests can grow again if replanted. Minerals cannot be replaced.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Land that is flat and raised high above sea level is called a ______.
questions.explanation: A plateau is high, fairly flat land.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Mount Elgon is found near which town?
questions.explanation: Mount Elgon rises near Mbale in eastern Uganda.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A piece of land completely surrounded by water is called an ______.
questions.explanation: Islands such as the Ssese Islands sit in Lake Victoria.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Lakes Albert, Edward and George lie in the ______.
questions.explanation: These lakes lie in the Western branch of the Rift Valley.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The River Nile leaves Lake Victoria at ______.
questions.explanation: The Nile begins its journey north at Jinja.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Low, wet land covered with papyrus is called a ______.
questions.explanation: Swamps hold water and support plants such as papyrus.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which instrument shows the direction from which the wind is blowing?
questions.explanation: A wind vane turns to point towards where the wind comes from.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A long period without rainfall is called a ______.
questions.explanation: A dry season is a long spell with little or no rain.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Rain that falls when moist air is forced to rise over a mountain is called ______ rainfall.
questions.explanation: Air rising over highlands cools and drops relief rainfall.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which vegetation grows in areas with heavy rainfall all year?
questions.explanation: Heavy, year-round rain supports thick rain forest.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Vegetation made up of tall grass with scattered trees is called ______.
questions.explanation: Savanna is grassland with a few scattered trees.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which farming method best reduces soil erosion on a slope?
options: A. Digging up and down the slope
B. Contour ploughing across the slope
questions.explanation: Ploughing across the slope slows running water.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which practice improves soil fertility naturally?
questions.explanation: Manure returns plant food to the soil.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which one is a use of water in the home?
questions.explanation: Water is used at home for cooking, washing and drinking.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which product comes from forests?
questions.explanation: Trees in forests are cut for timber.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Salt is traditionally mined at Lake ______ in western Uganda.
questions.explanation: Lake Katwe in Kasese is known for salt mining.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which problem is most likely where open mining takes place?
options: B. Large pits and destroyed land
questions.explanation: Open mining leaves pits and damages the land surface.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Growing crops only for the family to eat is called ______ farming.
questions.explanation: Subsistence farming feeds the farmer's own household.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A farmer who grows crops and also keeps animals practises ______ farming.
questions.explanation: Mixed farming combines crops and livestock on one farm.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why are tea and sugarcane usually grown on large plantations?
options: A. They need very little land
B. They need large areas and are processed in bulk
C. They grow in water only
questions.explanation: Plantation crops are grown in bulk to feed a factory nearby.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which fishing method is allowed and safe for the lake?
options: B. Using a net with legal mesh size
questions.explanation: Legal nets let young fish escape and grow.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Rearing fish in man-made ponds is called fish ______.
questions.explanation: Fish farming raises fish in ponds to increase supply.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Exchanging goods for other goods without money is called ______ trade.
questions.explanation: Barter trade exchanges goods directly.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Selling goods to other countries is called ______.
questions.explanation: Exportation is selling goods abroad.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which is an advantage of road transport over water transport in Uganda?
options: A. It reaches most parts of the country
B. It is only for heavy goods
D. It works only at night
questions.explanation: Roads reach nearly every district, unlike lakes and rivers.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which one is an example of print media?
questions.explanation: Newspapers are printed, so they are print media.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What is the main reason Uganda's population keeps growing?
options: A. Many people leave the country
B. Births are more than deaths
questions.explanation: When births outnumber deaths, population grows.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Houses built close together along a road form a ______ settlement.
questions.explanation: Linear settlements stretch in a line along a road or river.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which feature is more common in an urban area than a rural area?
options: B. Tall buildings and many shops
questions.explanation: Towns have many buildings, shops and services close together.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why do many young people move from villages to towns?
options: A. To look for jobs and services
B. Because villages have no land
questions.explanation: Towns offer jobs, schools and services that attract young people.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Who is the head of state of Uganda?
questions.explanation: The President is the head of state.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A person appointed to head a government ministry is called a ______.
questions.explanation: Ministers head ministries and are appointed by the President.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which one is a duty of every citizen?
questions.explanation: Citizens must obey the laws of the country.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which one helps to keep a community's culture alive?
questions.explanation: Dances, songs and ceremonies pass culture to the young.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The Karimojong keep moving with their animals mainly because ______.
options: B. they search for pasture and water
questions.explanation: In dry areas, herders move to find grass and water.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The Bachwezi are remembered in Ugandan history for ruling the empire of ______.
questions.explanation: The Bachwezi ruled the Bunyoro-Kitara empire.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The colonial power that ruled Uganda before independence was ______.
questions.explanation: Uganda was a British protectorate until 1962.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which practice protects a forest?
options: D. Cutting all trees at once
questions.explanation: Cutting a few trees and replanting keeps a forest alive.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A village wants clean water. Which project is most useful?
questions.explanation: A borehole directly solves the need for clean water.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: On a map of scale 1:100,000, 1 cm represents ______.
questions.explanation: 100,000 cm equals 1 km.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which direction lies between South and West?
questions.explanation: South West lies halfway between South and West.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: On a map, a small aeroplane symbol usually shows a ______.
questions.explanation: Map symbols stand for real features like airports.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Every good map should have a title, a key and a scale.
questions.explanation: Title, key and scale help a reader understand a map.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which programme helps Ugandan children attend primary school free of tuition?
questions.explanation: UPE was introduced so more children could attend primary school.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which resource can be used up completely and never replaced?
questions.explanation: Minerals such as copper are non-renewable: once mined, they are gone for good.
